question: Do successive bounded sessions produce useful gains after inheriting every strongest local construction?
seed: OS-generated 128-bit seed per session, recorded before search
order: Seeded count/arm ordering; sequential execution; identical session inputs for all arms
inheritance: Session 1 uses the working starts. Every later session inherits the exact maximum over every valid previous attempt and previous starts, including sub-gate gains. No baseline resets.
gain_gate: radius gain > max(1e-10, 1e-8 * session starting radius), computed with exact fractions

product_gate.meaning: At least one session 2 or 3 gain also clears the gate over its same-start full-budget polish control; a finite product readiness gate, not a success-probability or novelty estimate.

null_policy: Keep all attempts, solver failures/timeouts, initial states, hashes, measured CPU/wall time, and all unchanged counts. Partial sessions do not pass the gate.
comparisons: Equal wall allowances; report actual CPU and solver work. No causal agent benefit or solver superiority claim from this study. Adaptive-method comparison is a separate protocol.
release_gate: Independent geometric/provenance review, current external standing, named maintainer/review capacity and contributor onboarding are still required.
novelty: Public catalogue and pending witnesses need separate reconciliation; local yield is not record priority.
changes: Any method or budget change needs a new protocol/version before search; do not rewrite this package.
